title: Amino Acid Chemistry
objectives: Understand the structure and classification of amino acids
Describe the chemical properties and biological roles of amino acids
Explain peptide bond formation and protein structure levels
Analyze the metabolic pathways involving amino acids, including synthesis and degradation

overview.title: Amino Acid Overview
overview.content:
Amino acids are organic compounds containing both amino (-NH2) and carboxyl (-COOH) functional groups, along with a side chain (R group) specific to each amino acid. They are the building blocks of proteins and play critical roles in metabolism, signaling, and enzyme function. There are 20 standard amino acids that are incorporated into proteins, along with several non-standard amino acids with specialized functions.

Biological Significance

  • Protein Synthesis: Amino acids are polymerized into proteins through peptide bonds.
  • Metabolic Intermediates: Serve as precursors for neurotransmitters, hormones, and nucleotides.
  • Energy Production: Can be catabolized to produce ATP through various metabolic pathways.
  • pH Buffering: The amino and carboxyl groups allow amino acids to act as buffers.

Key Features

Standard Amino Acids

  • Nonpolar (Alanine, Valine, Leucine, Isoleucine)
  • Polar (Serine, Threonine, Asparagine, Glutamine)
  • Acidic (Aspartate, Glutamate)
  • Basic (Lysine, Arginine, Histidine)

Special Amino Acids

  • Proline (unique cyclic structure)
  • Cysteine (forms disulfide bonds)
  • Glycine (simplest amino acid)
  • Aromatic (Phenylalanine, Tyrosine, Tryptophan)

key_concepts.title: Key Concepts
key_concepts.content:
Zwitterion Formation

Definition: Amino acids exist as dipolar ions (zwitterions) at physiological pH, with a positive amino group and negative carboxyl group.

Peptide Bond

Formation: Condensation reaction between amino group of one amino acid and carboxyl group of another, releasing water.

Properties: Rigid, planar, and participates in hydrogen bonding in proteins.

Essential vs. Non-Essential

Essential: Cannot be synthesized by the body (9 amino acids, must be obtained from diet).

Non-Essential: Can be synthesized by the body (11 amino acids).

chemical_properties.title: Chemical Properties
chemical_properties.content:
Acid-Base Behavior

pKa Values: Amino acids have at least two pKa values (for -COOH and -NH3+ groups).

Isoelectric Point (pI): The pH at which the amino acid has no net charge.

Reactions

Ninhydrin Reaction: Used to detect amino acids, producing a purple color.

Disulfide Bond Formation: Oxidation of cysteine thiol groups forms cystine (important for protein structure).

Optical Activity

Chirality: All standard amino acids except glycine are chiral (L-configuration in proteins).

biological_roles.title: Biological Roles
biological_roles.content:
Protein Structure

Primary: Linear sequence of amino acids.

Secondary: Local folding (α-helices, β-sheets) stabilized by hydrogen bonds.

Tertiary: Overall 3D structure stabilized by various interactions.

Quaternary: Assembly of multiple polypeptide chains.

Metabolic Pathways

Transamination: Transfer of amino groups between amino acids and α-keto acids.

Urea Cycle: Elimination of excess nitrogen as urea.

Gluconeogenesis: Some amino acids can be converted to glucose.

Specialized Functions

Neurotransmitters: Glycine, glutamate, GABA, serotonin (from tryptophan).

Hormones: Thyroxine (from tyrosine), histamine (from histidine).

faqs.title: FAQs
faqs.content:
What makes proline unique among amino acids?+
Proline has a cyclic structure that introduces kinks in protein chains, often found in turns.
Why are cysteine residues important in proteins?+
Cysteine can form disulfide bonds that stabilize protein structure, especially in extracellular proteins.
What happens to amino acids in the body during starvation?+
Muscle proteins are broken down, and amino acids are used for gluconeogenesis or ketogenesis to provide energy.
How do essential and conditionally essential amino acids differ?+
Conditionally essential amino acids (e.g., arginine) are normally synthesized but may need to be supplemented during illness or stress.
